document.title: Themes: the Display menu switches between the project, user, and default colours
document.summary: The Display menu gets a Colours choice between the theme files and the built-in colours.
document.why: With a project theme and a home theme, only the project one showed, and there was [no way back](source:s1) to the built-in colours.

sources.label: PR #210
sources.title: Themes: the Display menu switches between the project, user, and default colours

groups.title: Load both theme files
groups.summary: `loadThemes` in `theme.ts` reads the repository file and the home file, and the payload sends both as `themes`. The `theme` command, `serve`, and `export` print one line per file they found.

attention.note: `loadThemes` now always parses the home file, and an invalid file still throws. Before, a valid project theme meant the home file was never read; now a broken `~/.comprehende/theme.json` stops `serve` and `export` in every repository. The error names the file, as it did for the project file.

notes.body: A repository at the home folder lists its one file as Project only.
Drops `path`, so a hosted export does not show home folder paths.

fileNotes.src/api/theme.ts: `loadTheme` returning one file becomes `loadThemes` returning a list with `source`.
fileNotes.src/api/theme.test.ts: Expects both files in order; an invalid home file now fails the load.
fileNotes.src/api/live.ts: `openReview` and `reviewPayload` carry the list instead of one theme.
fileNotes.src/api/export.test.ts: Checks the project entry of `themes`; the home file depends on the machine.
fileNotes.src/api/agent-md.test.ts: The sample review gets `themes: []` for the required field.
fileNotes.src/cli/args.ts: Help text says both files load and the Display menu switches.

groups.title: Colours choice in Display
groups.summary: `DisplayMenu` lists each theme in `themes` plus Default, and `App` applies the theme `pickThemeChoice` resolves from the stored choice.

attention.note: The choice is one localStorage key per origin, not per repository. A stored User or Default wins over a project theme written later, so a fresh project theme does not show until the user picks Project. With no stored choice, the page starts on the first theme, as before this change.

notes.body: `DisplayMenu` calls the same `pickThemeChoice`, so the check mark matches the page.

fileNotes.src/ui/lib/custom-theme.ts: Adds `ThemeChoice`, its storage key, and the `pickThemeChoice` fallback.
fileNotes.src/ui/lib/custom-theme.test.ts: New: fallback from a missing stored choice to project, user, then Default.
fileNotes.src/ui/lib/ThemeProvider.tsx: Holds the stored choice next to light and dark mode.
fileNotes.src/ui/App.tsx: Applies the chosen theme instead of the only one.
fileNotes.src/ui/components/DisplayMenu.tsx: Adds the Colours radio group above Theme; tooltip names colours.

groups.title: Docs name the Colours choice
groups.summary: The README and the skill's theme reference say both files load and the Display menu switches between them. The `.agents` file is the `pnpm sync:skill` copy of the `skills-next` file, so skip it.

fileNotes.README.md: Home file sentence and `theme` command row name the menu.
fileNotes.skills-next/comprehende/references/theme: Hand-over says a stored Colours choice can hide a new file.
fileNotes.scripts/ui-screenshots.ts: Comment only: the empty project theme is now the starting choice.

commits.subject: Themes: name the colour choice ThemeChoice, and say where to switch it
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Palette already names a light or dark token record in the theme schema.
The Display tooltip, README, and the skill's hand-over now name the
Colours choice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Themes: the Display menu switches between the project, user, and default colours
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The CLI now loads both .comprehende/theme.json files, the repository's
first. The payload carries both without paths, and the UI starts on the
first, so the default stays as before.
